speaker: Unknown
en: OK, hi.
zh: 好的,嗨。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right, I've got a lot to talk about, so I'm going to launch right into it here.
zh: 好了,我有很多要讲的内容,所以我这就直接开始了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So SWIX says that you only get to make one point at every talk, one key takeaway.
zh: SWIX 说,你在每次演讲中只能讲一个点,一个关键要点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I figured I'd just lead with that.
zh: 所以我想我就以此开场。

speaker: Unknown
en: My key point is personal AI code gen breaks traditional cloud infrastructure.
zh: 我的核心观点是个人 AI 代码生成打破了传统的云基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to clarify what I mean about that, the word personal here is doing a lot of work.
zh: 为了澄清我的意思,这里的「个人」一词承担了大量工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's load-bearing, as Claude would say.
zh: 它是承重的,正如 Claude 会说的那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: My point is that if we want to see this future where everyone has personal apps and can personalize the apps that they run, the infrastructure we're using today for software in general is not the right thing and we need something completely different.
zh: 我的观点是,如果我们想要看到这样一个未来,每个人都拥有个人应用程序并且可以个性化他们运行的应用程序,那么我们今天通用的软件基础设施就不是正确的东西,我们需要完全不同的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So to explain what I mean.
zh: 所以为了解释我的意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think about the way that software is produced and distributed today.
zh: 思考一下软件今天的生产和分发方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a developer in an ivory tower who builds an app and then sends it down to the people, the users who use the app.
zh: 你有一个身处象牙塔中的开发者构建了一个应用程序,然后把它发送给人们,使用该应用程序的用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And many of them are happy with it, but some of them are not.
zh: 他们中的许多人对此很满意,但有些人不满意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of them say, this app needs some additional features for my use case.
zh: 有些人说,这个应用程序需要针对我的用例增加一些额外功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they go to the developer and they say, oh, great developer, will you please grant my feature request?
zh: 于是他们去找开发者并说,哦,伟大的开发者,请你批准我的功能请求好吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Your app is literally unusable without it.
zh: 没有它你的应用程序简直无法使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so then the developer's representative, the product manager, takes these feature requests and files them into JIRA where they are never seen again.
zh: 然后开发者的代表,产品经理,接收这些功能请求并将它们归档到 JIRA 中,从此它们就再也没人看过了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But sometimes, sometimes the product manager sees the feature request and says, ah, you know, I want that too.
zh: 但有时,有时产品经理看到了功能请求并说,啊,你知道,我也想要那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then that feature request goes onto the roadmap and the developer works on it.
zh: 然后那个功能请求就进入了路线图,开发者开始着手处理它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the developer is implementing all these features, features that, you know, each one is only used by a small subset of users.
zh: 开发者正在实现所有这些功能,这些功能,你知道,每一个都只被一小部分用户使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And each one is adding all these if statements, their code, and making things messy.
zh: 每一个都在代码中添加了所有的这些 if 语句,使事情变得混乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they don't like it because the code base is becoming a mess.
zh: 他们不喜欢这样,因为代码库变得一团糟。

speaker: Unknown
en: And each of these features are really kind of boring to implement.
zh: 这些功能中的每一个实现起来都真的很无聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the developer says, ah, I know what I need to do.
zh: 开发者说,啊,我知道我需要做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need a rewrite.
zh: 我们需要一次重写。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need a new architecture that has a plugin system.
zh: 我们需要一个新的具有插件系统的架构。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then every one of these features can be a plugin and it can be nice and clean and easy to build and the core can stay clean.
zh: 然后这些功能中的每一个都可以是一个插件,它可以变得整洁、干净且易于构建,核心也能保持整洁。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the developer goes off and starts working on the new architecture with the plugin system.
zh: 所以开发者离开并开始研究带有插件系统的新架构。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are still feature requests coming in.
zh: 功能请求仍然源源不断。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the developer says, well, we can't do those features yet because we need the plugin system.
zh: 开发者说,嗯,我们还不能做这些功能,因为我们需要插件系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: This will be so much easier once we have the plugin system.
zh: 一旦我们有了插件系统,这就容易多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we do it now, we're just delaying that and we'll just have to redo it later anyway.
zh: 如果我们现在做,只是在推迟这件事,而且反正以后我们也得重做一遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: The years go by, and the new architecture is not ready yet, and none of the features are being implemented, and people are saying, what are they doing?
zh: 几年过去了,新架构还没准备好,没有任何功能被实现,人们都在说,他们在做什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: This developer has given up their product, and everybody is sad.
zh: 这个开发者已经放弃了他们的产品,每个人都很伤心。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, AI seems to present a new alternative to this.
zh: 所以,AI 似乎为此提供了一个新的替代方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: What if the developer could
zh: 如果开发者能够

speaker: Unknown
en: Create their app, the first version of their app, give it to the users, and the users, if they need a new feature, could say, I could ask their AI agent to write that feature just for them, add it to the app.
zh: 创建他们的应用程序,应用程序的第一个版本,把它交给用户,如果用户需要新功能,可以说,我可以让他们的 AI 智能体专门为他们编写那个功能,将其添加到应用程序中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then everyone gets the features they need, no one is bogged down in everyone else's features, and the developer gets to keep the core app nice and clean and beautiful.
zh: 这样每个人都得到了他们需要的功能,没有人被其他人的功能拖累,开发者也能保持核心应用程序的整洁、干净和美观。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's a problem with this, which is that none of the infrastructure we build software on today is remotely designed for this.
zh: 但这有一个问题,那就是我们今天构建软件所用的基础设施都不是为此设计的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've got Apple and Google for the past 15 years gatekeeping their systems to the point where there's five companies that can build mobile apps now because everyone else has been banned.
zh: 你看看 Apple 和 Google,在过去 15 年里严防死守他们的系统,以至于现在只有五家公司能构建移动应用程序,因为其他人都被封禁了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's almost easier in the United States to buy a gun than it is to get access to your own phone to install unsigned software.
zh: 在美国,搞到一把枪几乎比获得你自己手机的访问权限以安装未签名的软件还要容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: You go to Google and you say, I want to install unsigned software.
zh: 你去找 Google 并说,我想安装未签名的软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now they're going to say, oh, whoa, hold on, buddy.
zh: 然后他们会说,哦,哇,等一下,伙计。

speaker: Unknown
en: You seem upset.
zh: 你看起来很激动。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should go home and think about this.
zh: 你应该回家先冷静一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you still want that unsigned software in 24 hours, then you can come back and talk to us.
zh: 如果你在 24 小时后仍然想要那个未签名的软件,那你再回来找我们谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fortunately, we have a workaround for all of that, which is the web.
zh: 幸运的是,我们针对所有这一切有一个变通方法,那就是网络。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the web, everyone can build whatever they want, and it turns out it's fine.
zh: 在网络上,每个人都可以构建他们想要的任何东西,结果证明这没问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not the security disaster that Apple and Google keep telling us would happen.
zh: 这并没有发生 Apple 和 Google 一直告诉我们会发生的那些安全灾难。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can build whatever you want on the web, but there's a different problem on the web, which is that for the past 25 years of cloud architecture, we've been running in the wrong direction.
zh: 所以你可以在网络上构建你想要的任何东西,但网络有一个不同的问题,那就是在过去的 25 年云架构中,我们一直在错误的方向上奔跑。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you distribute a web app,
zh: 当你分发一个网络应用程序时,

speaker: Unknown
en: You run it on your own server.
zh: 你在你自己的服务器上运行它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Put it on your server and then users send requests to your server where the one version of your app, the one blessed version, runs for every single user.
zh: 把它放在你的服务器上,然后用户向你的服务器发送请求,在那里,你的应用程序的一个版本,那个经过核准的版本,为每一个用户运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's convenient for developers.
zh: 所以这对开发者来说很方便。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why we've done it is so the developer can make sure things stay updated and everyone's on the same version.
zh: 这就是我们这样做的原因,以便开发者可以确保事物保持更新,并且每个人都在同一个版本上。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it obviously means that users cannot customize their apps.
zh: 但这显然意味着用户无法定制他们的应用程序。

speaker: Unknown
en: So...
zh: 所以……

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, last year, vibe coding comes along, and we have all these vibe coding platforms out there, and most of them are targeting web apps because that's the easy thing to target, but they're all targeting this existing infrastructure, which is actually not the right way to do it.
zh: 你知道,去年,vibe coding 出现了,我们那里有所有这些 vibe coding 平台,其中大多数都针对 Web 应用程序,因为那是很容易针对的目标,但它们都针对这种现有的基础设施,这实际上不是做这件事的正确方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need something entirely different, and hence my point.
zh: 我们需要一些完全不同的东西,因此我有这个观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you like how the word breaks kind of wiggles every now and then?
zh: 你喜欢单词换行时不时摆动的方式吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: That was something Claude put in there, and it was so stupid, I just had to keep it.
zh: 那是 Claude 放在那里的东西,太愚蠢了,我只好保留它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to know where in Claude's training data it learned that you could make words wiggle to give them emphasis, because I understand the red, I understand the underline, but the wiggle, I don't think that's from humans.
zh: 我想知道在 Claude 的训练数据中的哪里,它学会了你可以让单词摆动来强调它们,因为我理解红色,我理解下划线,但是摆动,我不认为那是来自人类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's an AI original.
zh: 我认为那是 AI 的原创。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is ASI, folks.
zh: 这是 ASI,各位。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's beyond my puny human brain's ability to comprehend.
zh: 这超出了我微小的人类大脑的理解能力。

zh: 这不像你典型的 vibe coding 环境,你在那里将应用程序部署到网页。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

en: If I want multiple slide decks, I make multiple instances of the gadget, one for each.

speaker: Unknown
en: And because each gadget is just the one thing that you want to share, that means that the platform can implement the sharing model and the access control such that the gadget itself can't possibly get that wrong.
zh: 而且因为每个小工具只是你想要分享的一件事，这意味着平台可以实现分享模型和访问控制，这样小工具本身就不可能搞错。

en: And the answer to that is it doesn't really matter because of the way this environment is set up.
zh: 答案是这其实并不重要，因为这个环境的设置方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the UI that you see for the app here is running inside a null origin iframe sandbox with content security policy set so that it basically cannot talk to anything, any of the rest of the world, can't access any cookies, so on.
zh: 所以你在这里为应用看到的 UI 运行在一个 null origin iframe 沙箱中，并设置了内容安全策略，因此它基本上无法与任何事物、世界的其余部分对话，无法访问任何 cookie，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: The only thing it can do is post message to the parent frame.
zh: 它唯一能做的就是向父 frame 发送消息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And through that post message channel, we set up a Captain Web RPC session, which forwards onto the server and all the way back to the server code for this gadget, which is this code here, which is written as a durable object on Cloudflare Workers.
zh: 并且通过那个消息通道，我们建立了一个 Captain Web RPC 会话，它转发到服务器并一直传回这个小工具的服务器代码，也就是这里的这段代码，它是作为 Cloudflare Workers 上的 durable object 编写的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And basically that means, so this server code runs in a dynamic worker sandbox on the server side where it too is prevented from talking to any of the rest of the world.
zh: 基本上这意味着，所以这个服务器代码运行在服务器端的动态 worker 沙箱中，在那里它也被禁止与世界的其余部分对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now we've set up this environment where there's a vibe-coded client and a vibe-coded server, and they can only talk to each other and produce the UI for the user.
zh: 所以现在我们建立了一个环境，其中有一个 vibe coding 的客户端和一个 vibe coding 的服务器，它们只能彼此对话并为用户生成 UI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you have an XSS bug, it actually doesn't end up mattering because these can't leak anything.
zh: 所以如果你有一个 XSS 漏洞，它实际上并不重要，因为这些无法泄露任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're prevented from doing so.
zh: 它们被禁止这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And basically, there is no security bug you can have in this code that matters.
zh: 基本上，在这段代码中你不可能有任何重要的安全漏洞。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that makes it safe to go and do things.
zh: 这使得去做事情是安全的。

en: So there's a whole lot that I would like to talk about that I won't have time for here, unfortunately.

speaker: Unknown
en: For instance, we created a whole system by which these apps can talk to external services in a safe way, but I could give two more talks about that.
zh: 例如，我们创建了一整套系统，通过这些应用可以安全地与外部服务对话，但我可以就那个主题再讲两场。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of stuff here.
zh: 这里有很多东西。

en: So everything you see here is built on, everything except for the LLM is built on Cloudflare workers.
zh: 所以你在这里看到的一切都是基于……除了 LLM 之外的一切都是基于 Cloudflare workers 构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people don't know this, but you can actually build complex apps on workers.
zh: 很多人不知道这一点，但你实际上可以在 workers 上构建复杂的应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are no containers involved here.
zh: 这里不涉及容器。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's just dynamic workers.
zh: 只有动态 workers。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no database involved.
zh: 这里不涉及数据库。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just uses durable objects.
zh: 它只使用 durable objects。

speaker: Unknown
en: And furthermore, all of this is actually running locally on my laptop, which is why it doesn't matter that the internet didn't work.
zh: 此外，所有这些都实际上运行在本地我的笔记本电脑上，这就是为什么网络断了也没关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is all running on WorkerD, which is our open source runtime.
zh: 所以这一切都运行在 WorkerD 上，这是我们的开源运行时。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people don't know this.
zh: 很多人不知道这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Cloudflare Workers runtime is open source.
zh: Cloudflare Workers 运行时是开源的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can self-host it.
